texts.heading: Priya
texts.text: I have worked from my kitchen table for three years and I would not go back. I save two hours a day on commuting, and my concentration is far better without colleagues interrupting. People worry about loneliness, but I see my friends more now than I did before.

texts.heading: Daniel
texts.text: Everyone praises the freedom, yet I miss the office. Ideas come from casual conversations by the coffee machine, and those do not survive on video calls. I accept that the commute was tiresome, but it also gave me a boundary between work and home.

texts.heading: Hannah
texts.text: For my team the main gain is flexibility. Parents can collect children and no one has to spend a fortune on rent in the city. The loss is spontaneity, but we meet in person once a month, which seems to be enough to keep us together.

texts.heading: Marcus
texts.text: Companies like remote work because it cuts costs, not because it makes people happy. I find it isolating, and younger staff especially lose out because they learn by watching others. Meeting monthly is not a real substitute for daily contact.
